richText: Configuration values control application settings without changing Java source.
Spring Boot loads application.properties or application.yml from standard locations, including the classpath root and external configuration locations.
In the project, src/main/resources is the usual location for a packaged configuration file.
Properties files use key=value lines. YAML uses indentation for nested values.
At the same location, application.properties takes precedence over YAML if both exist.

example.title: Set the server port
description: Use one of these equivalent configurations in src/main/resources.
example.code:
# application.properties
server.port=8081

# Equivalent application.yml
server:
  port: 8081
explanation: Choose one file format for this setting.
A servlet web application reads server.port during startup and listens on port 8081 unless another source overrides it.

richText: For ordinary runtime settings, environment variables override configuration files, and command-line arguments override environment variables. Other property sources also exist.
SERVER_PORT is the environment-variable form of server.port.
JVM options go before -jar. Application arguments go after the JAR name.
Store credentials outside committed configuration files. A profile-specific file does not hide its contents.

example.title: Override the server port at startup
description: Assume the packaged file sets server.port=8081 and the JAR is target/demo.jar.
explanation: This is a Unix shell command.
The command-line value 9091 overrides both the environment value 9090 and the file value 8081.
-Xmx512m sets the JVM’s maximum heap size. It is not a Spring property.
